question: Does the proposed Comments persistence and history API remain the best scalable target after a final adversarial ownership, synchronization, and product-parity pass?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; repeated first-principles hard-cut; independent API and history attacks; current-source reconciliation
trigger: User requested a last pass to make sure the Comments history design missed nothing material.
requirements: Preserve published conversations independently from document undo, while retaining exact attachment recovery when the paired checkpoint supports it.
Keep one live location owner, one semantic conversation owner, and no mandatory activity log, tombstone store, or Authored dependency.
Bind saved targets, document data, and optional local history to one validated checkpoint identity without eager full-cohort serialization.
Make initialization, version restore, live synchronization, collaboration admission, and durable mutation failure semantics explicit rather than conflating them.
Expose only attachment states the package can prove, keep authorization application-owned, and state the text-only target scope until non-text targets have a durable primitive.
Record the correction without implementing or teaching an unselected public API.
evidenceReuse: Reused the prior current-source inventory, 29 focused unit/component passes, one Chromium live-undo pass, reload-recovery probe, and frozen 1/100/1000/10000-anchor serialization probe. Re-read the current Comments record, subscription, setThreads, copied UI, multi-editor proof consumer, Plite anchor/history codecs, Authored identity, and Yjs admission path. Rechecked official Google comments documentation for commenter resolution permission and non-text targets. No unchanged runtime proof was rerun.
summary: Defer the public API and supersede the earlier save({ids?}) sketch. Keep Comments as the current conversation owner, but delete the copied mapped Range from live CommentThread records: a private native Anchor is the sole location owner and range(id) is its projection. The next design must bind document, selected ranges, and optional history in one versioned checkpoint; restore through a fresh editor or staged atomic apply; separate quiescent load from ordered live patches; and use one awaitable durable-mutation boundary. The mandatory activity log and tombstone store remain cut.
alternatives: Keep a mapped Range inside each live CommentThread: reject; it duplicates the native Anchor, rewrites conversation records on document edits, and makes location movement look like semantic data churn.
Call save({ids: change.ids}) from subscribeThreads: reject; one edit can affect the full 10000-anchor cohort, and deferred serialization can pair an anchor with the wrong document revision.

Take independent document, thread, and HistoryJSON reads: reject as an exact-recovery contract; current codecs carry no shared durable checkpoint identity and cannot reject every structurally valid wrong-document combination.
Require history/anchor restore to work in any order: cut absent a real consumer; choose one explicit load order inside fresh-editor or staged atomic checkpoint application.

Use setThreads for both checkpoint restore and live multi-editor refresh: reject; a remote editor's target cannot replace a locally advanced target safely. Keep wholesale load quiescent and design an ordered patch/action path only if live synchronization is in scope.

Keep synchronous resolve/delete booleans while claiming server-first authorization: reject; copied UI treats a Promise as success. Use one awaitable durable-mutation command/result boundary or explicitly specify optimistic reconciliation.

Infer deleted versus unavailable from range(id) returning null or a collapsed range: reject; authored projection and checkpoint mismatch produce the same observation. Expose provenance or use neutral wording.

Claim Google-style comment parity with range and change targets: reject; Google documents comments on images and other non-text targets. Keep this design explicitly text-only until a durable non-text primitive is justified.

Restore persisted local undo after collaborative room admission by default: reject; without binding to the collaboration baseline and replaying every intervening change, structurally valid coordinates can be wrong.
Mandatory append-only CommentActivity, duplicate tombstones, or an Authored requirement: continue to reject; none repairs checkpoint identity and each adds an unjustified owner.
proofLimits: This is a design correction, not product implementation. The current codec still fails exact ordinary deleted-span recovery after reload, and the proposed joint checkpoint codec does not exist. The 10000-authored-anchor full-cohort candidate remains over the 100 ms gate; the passing selective measurement excludes the missing recovery payload and cannot approve save({ids}). No atomic restore, wrong-checkpoint rejection, Yjs-baseline admission, ordered live patch, async authorization failure, attachment-provenance, non-text target, or Google ordinary-comment deletion behavior has runtime proof. Google and Notion version-restore internals remain unverified. Earlier live tests were not rerun because their covered source and claim did not change.
